bull_bear.body: Priorities: 1) fund committed capex (INR220Cr), 2) retain dry powder (INR2,437M net cash) for inorganic acquisitions, 3) dividend payout of 35% of face value (INR3.5/share); no debt used, debt-free balance sheet maintained
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Global supply chain disruptions; geopolitical volatility affecting export markets; delay in BOE display product qualification; slower-than-expected ramp-up of new WPI programs; currency fluctuations impacting export profitability
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, bullish on FY27; emphasized disciplined execution, margin expansion, and strategic patience in export and inorganic growth; reiterated 26-year track record of outperformance; tone was assertive on technology leadership and operational excellence
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Export intensity is understated in consolidated figures — SJS standalone export contribution is significantly higher than reported due to SDPL/WPI being domestic-focused; BOE partnership is not just about displays but about vertical integration of aesthetic + electronic functions, positioning SJS as a holistic cabin experience partner
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free on long-term debt across FY25, FY26 and Q1FY27 (all zero), with total debt of only Rs 93 Mn at Q1FY27 against cash and cash equivalents of Rs 3,381 Mn, giving net cash of Rs 3,287.7 Mn as on 30th June 2026.
- ICRA upgraded SJS long term funds rating to AA- (Positive) from AA- (Stable); strong cash flow generation is stated as supporting expansion initiatives.
- ROCE progression of 25% (FY25), 36% (FY26), 37% (Q1FY27) and ROE of 17%, 20%, 20%; deck text states ROE and ROCE improved to 20.3% and 37.2%.
- FCFF of Rs 1,233 Mn (FY25), Rs 1,427 Mn (FY26) and Rs 838 Mn (Q1FY27); total equity of Rs 9,583 Mn at Q1FY27.
- The deck makes no mention of dividend, buyback or a stated payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Design-to-delivery model and R&D/NPD capabilities (135-member NPD team) enabling entry into sophisticated, high-entry-barrier product categories with few competitors
- Manages over 17,500 SKUs with a diversified product portfolio, plant locations and customer base that spreads geographic and customer-concentration risk
- Long-standing customer relationships with key OEMs, some spanning nearly two decades
- Equipment/machinery flexibility across production lines and strict quality control at every stage to keep rejection rates low and avoid order delays
- AA-(Positive) long-term funds credit rating by ICRA, upgraded during the year from AA-(Stable)
- Technology Licence-cum-Supply Agreement with BOE Varitronix (BOEVX), Hong Kong for optical bonding and assembly of automotive display systems in India
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macro-economic / geopolitical risk — Heightened global conflicts, economic downturns, inflation, and supply chain disruptions present critical risks that may constrain client demand, strain end-user industries, and limit export markets, affecting the Company's growth; mitigated by generating sales from a wide customer base across multiple geographic areas and maintaining a diversified plant footprint.
- Competition risk — The Company faces intense competition from both established and unorganised industry players; failure to consistently provide high-quality, innovative items could lead to a decline in market share and profitability. Mitigated by a strong brand identity, ability to manage over 17,500 SKUs, and a design-to-delivery model with R&D capabilities that has enabled entry into sophisticated categories with high entry barriers and few competitors.
- Operational risk — Business and financial success may suffer from delays in day-to-day operations, poor work management, inability to meet varied customer demands, failure to deliver quality products on time, or high rejection rates; mitigated by equipment/machinery flexibility across production lines, regular process reviews, capacity planning and strict quality-control inspection.
- Technology risk — Failure to adapt to new technological developments may affect revenue and profit margins; the Company addresses this through continuous investment in advanced technologies (e.g., the BOE Varitronix TLA for optical bonding/display systems) and a 135-member NPD team that identifies emerging trends.
- Customer concentration / customer risk — Loss of key customers due to unforeseen events could negatively impact reputation and revenue growth; the risk is mitigated through market expansion and new customer acquisition, and on a consolidated basis no single customer accounts for more than 16-17% of total revenue.
- Currency / foreign exchange risk — Foreign exchange risk arises from the mix of importing raw materials and exporting finished goods; adverse exchange rate movements could reduce revenue or increase input costs and impact margins. Only partially managed through a natural hedge from the import/export mix, as no formal hedging arrangements were executed during the year.
- Crude oil / input cost risk — Fluctuations in crude oil prices, driven by geopolitical tensions, macroeconomic events and high inflation, could affect margins; mitigated by long-standing supplier relationships with alternative options, negotiated price pass-through to customers after a brief delay, and Value Analysis/Value Engineering, energy conservation and waste reduction initiatives.
- Talent / human capital risk — Shortage of skilled workers or difficulty retaining key employees could affect operations; managed through skills development, training, employee engagement programmes and an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) to incentivise and retain high performers.
- Cybersecurity and fraud risk — Increasing digitalisation and reliance on technology systems expose the Company to cybersecurity incidents, data breaches, system disruptions and fraudulent activities that could impact business continuity, compromise sensitive information, and lead to financial or reputational loss; addressed through a structured cybersecurity framework, access controls, periodic monitoring and employee awareness programmes.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: 2-wheeler: 38.3% of FY26 revenue, grew 4x industry; passenger vehicle: 41.7% of FY26 revenue, grew 3x industry; consumer & others: 20% of FY26 revenue, rationalized low-margin products, new high-margin programs ramping up
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Operates in the high value-add aesthetics market across multiple consumer-oriented end industries, focused on premium aesthetic products and innovative designs, with in-house design and R&D capabilities.
- Describes itself as partner, co-creator and supplier of choice to several leading OEMs in the automotive and consumer durables industry; deck's timeline notes that on listing in Nov-21 SJS 'is the only listed company in India in this space'.
- Claims outperformance of industry growth for the 27th consecutive quarter; Q1FY27 automotive growth of 32.4% YoY versus 21.7% YoY for the automotive (2W+PV) industry production volumes, described as 1.5x growth v/s industry.
- SJS in-house R&D centre achieved recognition by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order book] Current order book to be executed in FY27 is over 88% of FY27 forecasted revenue; SJS expects to outperform underlying industry growth by 1.5-2x.
- [Exceptional item] Reported PAT includes a Rs 241.7 Mn exceptional gain — a one-time post-tax gain on sale of the Bangalore old facility, which was not in use since 2019.
- [Ownership] Aug'23 saw a stake sale of ~30% by PE promoter Everstone Capital, which had acquired a majority stake in 2015 with Serigraph exiting.
- [Governance] Board is chaired by a Non-Executive Chairman & Independent Director; the ESG annexure reports 57.14% independent board of directors and 16.7% founder board members.
- [Outlook wording] The FY27 outlook bullet reads 'Continue to maintain robust margin profile of business for FY26' — the deck refers to FY26 in an FY27 outlook slide.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: SJS designs and manufactures decorative aesthetic and functional components - decals, domes/badges, overlays, 2D/3D dials/appliques, IML/IMD/IMF parts, chrome-plated and painted components, lens mask assemblies and optical plastics - primarily for two-wheeler and passenger-vehicle OEMs and Tier-1 auto component makers. It also serves consumer appliance makers (washing machines, refrigerators, dishwashers, ceiling fans, water purifiers, consumer electricals, sanitaryware) and other industries such as medical and farm equipment. The company is entering cover glass and display systems as a new product category.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Branding & Aesthetic Enhancements:** Self-adhesive labels (decals and body graphics), 2D and 3D appliques and dials, 3D luxury badges, domes, overlays and aluminium badges, Kromex badges, Capacitive overlays
- **Advanced Moulding & Finishing:** In-mould labels (IML), In-mould decorations (IMD), IMF, Illuminated Logos, Chrome-plated, printed and painted injection-moulded plastic parts
- **Precision Optical & Functional Components:** Lens mask assemblies, Optical plastics, Cover Glass & Displays (new category being added)
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- SJS Decoplast Private Limited (formerly Exotech Plastics Private Limited) — subsidiary: Wholly-owned (100%) subsidiary, acquired 5th April 2021; manufacturing operations contributing to the automotive/consumer aesthetics portfolio; hosts the chrome plating and painting capacity expansion; transacts with the parent for sale/purchase of goods and dividend.
- Walter Pack Automotive Products India Private Limited (WPI) — subsidiary: 90.1%-owned subsidiary, acquired 4th July 2023; diversified the group's portfolio across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and consumer segments and strengthened technology capabilities in IMD, IMF and IML; transacts with the parent for sale/purchase of goods.
- Plastoranger Advanced Technologies Private Limited — subsidiary: Was a wholly-owned subsidiary of Walter Pack Automotive Products India Private Limited; amalgamated with WPI (the holding company) during the year pursuant to an order of the Regional Director under Section 233 read with Rule 25(5) of the Companies Act, 2013, and no longer exists as a separate entity.
- SJS Foundation — related party: A trust that is a related party of the Company (CSR-related trust); the Company does not have any holding/ultimate holding company, and has no associate or joint venture as at the end of the financial year.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 30.3% due to premium product mix (24% of revenue from new-gen products), higher export contribution (60.5% YoY growth), operational efficiencies, and back-to-back cost pass-throughs on chrome plating inputs; polymer cost inflation mitigated by annual product refresh pricing
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: outperform industry by 1.5x–2x in FY27; margin: target 27–28% long-term; order inflow: strong pipeline across global OEMs; capex/commissioning: INR145Cr total capex planned over FY26–FY28 (INR80Cr done in FY26), including INR45Cr Bangalore expansion (20% capacity), INR100Cr SDPL chrome greenfield (commissioning complete), and display facility in Hosur (equipment ordered, production expected end-FY27/early-FY28)
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: BOE Varitronix optical display partnership (cover glass, TFT bonding) to unlock $4B global market; export expansion into Germany, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, South Korea; inorganic acquisitions in NA, SEA, India targeting margin-accretive players
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scaling: increase scale through capacity expansion and capabilities to support rising customer demand
- Innovating: focus on development of new technologies and advanced products, moving up the value chain into IMD/IML, IMF, hot stamping, optical plastics/cover glass and displays, and advanced decorative applications
- Expanding: grow mega accounts and increase global presence through exports, new geographies and deepened OEM relationships
- Mergers & Acquisitions: increasing focus on exploring value-accretive acquisitions that add new technologies, enhance market access and strengthen the customer base, complementing organic growth
- Build capabilities in adjacent and emerging aesthetic segments (similar to the earlier expansion into IMD/IML, IMF, chrome plating and painted components) to further diversify the product portfolio
- Accelerate presence in consumer-oriented industries including appliances and electricals, while expanding into high-potential global markets such as North America, Europe and Southeast Asia
- Continue to evaluate strategic inorganic opportunities to access advanced technologies, expand into newer markets, and widen the customer base
- Establish an end-to-end optical cover glass manufacturing line with specialised coatings (anti-glare, anti-reflection, anti-fingerprint) to transition from traditional products to high-value, technology-driven products (cover glass, digital displays, IMD/IML components, chrome-plated parts), boosting kit value
- The Company's stated capital management policy is to maintain a stable and strong capital base with a focus on total equity, in order to sustain investor, creditor and market confidence and to fund future development and growth of the business, while monitoring return on capital and the level of dividends paid on equity shares. The stated objective in managing capital is to maintain an optimal capital structure that maximises shareholder value while safeguarding the Company's ability to continue as a going concern; no changes were made to this policy during the year. Consistent with this, the Board recommended a final dividend for the year, to be declared at the AGM, reflecting an intent to reward shareholders alongside continued reinvestment in capacity expansion and organic/inorganic growth.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: SJS operates four existing manufacturing facilities across Bengaluru, Pune and Gurugram, with two new facilities coming up at Pune and Hosur to support capacity expansion and entry into a new product category. At SJS Decoplast (Pune), a chrome plating and painting capacity expansion (overall capex ~Rs 1,000 Mn) has been set up and is in its final stage of commissioning. A greenfield cover glass and automotive display facility is being established at Hosur (Phase I capital outlay ~Rs 650 Mn, including display system assembly); equipment has been ordered and revenue contribution is expected to begin from FY 2027-28. Capacity is also being expanded at the SJS (Bengaluru) plant (capex of Rs 400-450 Mn) to cater to a significant new business opportunity, with the expansion progressing well. Total capex investment across these projects was Rs 822.4 Mn (consolidated) in FY26. Growth has also come inorganically: the SJS Decoplast acquisition delivered revenue growth of 3.5x between FY 2020-21 and FY 2025-26, and the integration of Walter Pack India (WPI) diversified the portfolio across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and consumer segments and strengthened IMD/IMF/IML technology capabilities; management continues to evaluate further value-accretive M&A opportunities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian decorative aesthetics industry estimated at ~Rs 49.2 billion in FY26, reflecting ~20% CAGR from FY 2020-21 amid premiumization across end-user segments, outpacing underlying volume growth in two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and durables (10-12% CAGR), driven by EV-specific trims, advanced coatings and manufacturing localisation (Source: Equity Edge Research)
- EV surge is a key market driver: electric models demand 1.5-2x higher aesthetic content (decals, chrome, IML) versus ICE vehicles, bolstered by PLI schemes and export growth
- Premiumization in appliances and sanitaryware, where durable, glossy finishes meet regulatory pushes for corrosion resistance and eco-compliance, is a growth driver
- Farm equipment mechanisation and capacity ramps are amplifying need for customised surface solutions amid a fragmented yet consolidating supply chain
- Industry is fragmented among niche specialists delivering end-to-end design-to-production; leaders with zero-debt profiles and EV-ready capabilities gain margin resilience and share in a globally underpenetrated, consolidating market
- Two-wheeler industry recorded highest-ever domestic sales in FY26 (10.7% growth), supported by GST 2.0, repo-rate cuts and income tax relief boosting consumer sentiment, with premiumisation (higher engine capacity, features) and rising EV segment uptick as sub-trends
- Passenger vehicle industry recorded highest-ever annual sales in FY26 (7.9% growth), with stronger growth in the second half of the year
- Rising demand for optical plastics/cover glass and display systems, as OEMs focus on design differentiation and higher content per vehicle, is supporting SJS's move into cover-glass and display manufacturing
- PV segment kit value is expected to grow from a legacy kit value of Rs 1,200-1,500 per vehicle, to a current kit value of Rs 3,500-5,000 per vehicle, with future kit value guided at 5-8x growth over the legacy level, as the product mix shifts to cover glass, digital displays, IMD/IML components and chrome-plated parts

risks.note: Heightened global conflicts, economic downturns, inflation, and supply chain disruptions present critical risks that may constrain client demand, strain end-user industries, and limit export markets, affecting the Company's growth; mitigated by generating sales from a wide customer base across multiple geographic areas and maintaining a diversified plant footprint.

The Company faces intense competition from both established and unorganised industry players; failure to consistently provide high-quality, innovative items could lead to a decline in market share and profitability. Mitigated by a strong brand identity, ability to manage over 17,500 SKUs, and a design-to-delivery model with R&D capabilities that has enabled entry into sophisticated categories with high entry barriers and few competitors.

Business and financial success may suffer from delays in day-to-day operations, poor work management, inability to meet varied customer demands, failure to deliver quality products on time, or high rejection rates; mitigated by equipment/machinery flexibility across production lines, regular process reviews, capacity planning and strict quality-control inspection.

Failure to adapt to new technological developments may affect revenue and profit margins; the Company addresses this through continuous investment in advanced technologies (e.g., the BOE Varitronix TLA for optical bonding/display systems) and a 135-member NPD team that identifies emerging trends.

Loss of key customers due to unforeseen events could negatively impact reputation and revenue growth; the risk is mitigated through market expansion and new customer acquisition, and on a consolidated basis no single customer accounts for more than 16-17% of total revenue.

Foreign exchange risk arises from the mix of importing raw materials and exporting finished goods; adverse exchange rate movements could reduce revenue or increase input costs and impact margins. Only partially managed through a natural hedge from the import/export mix, as no formal hedging arrangements were executed during the year.

Fluctuations in crude oil prices, driven by geopolitical tensions, macroeconomic events and high inflation, could affect margins; mitigated by long-standing supplier relationships with alternative options, negotiated price pass-through to customers after a brief delay, and Value Analysis/Value Engineering, energy conservation and waste reduction initiatives.

Shortage of skilled workers or difficulty retaining key employees could affect operations; managed through skills development, training, employee engagement programmes and an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) to incentivise and retain high performers.

Increasing digitalisation and reliance on technology systems expose the Company to cybersecurity incidents, data breaches, system disruptions and fraudulent activities that could impact business continuity, compromise sensitive information, and lead to financial or reputational loss; addressed through a structured cybersecurity framework, access controls, periodic monitoring and employee awareness programmes.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: SJS is a decorative-aesthetics and functional-component manufacturer with 39 years of expertise, supplying automotive (2W/PV) and consumer-appliance OEMs in India and abroad.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SJS designs and manufactures decorative aesthetic and functional components - decals, domes/badges, overlays, 2D/3D dials/appliques, IML/IMD/IMF parts, chrome-plated and painted components, lens mask assemblies and optical plastics - primarily for two-wheeler and passenger-vehicle OEMs and Tier-1 auto component makers. It also serves consumer appliance makers (washing machines, refrigerators, dishwashers, ceiling fans, water purifiers, consumer electricals, sanitaryware) and other industries such as medical and farm equipment. The company is entering cover glass and display systems as a new product category.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- SJS Decoplast Private Limited (formerly Exotech Plastics Private Limited) — subsidiary: Wholly-owned (100%) subsidiary, acquired 5th April 2021; manufacturing operations contributing to the automotive/consumer aesthetics portfolio; hosts the chrome plating and painting capacity expansion; transacts with the parent for sale/purchase of goods and dividend.
- Walter Pack Automotive Products India Private Limited (WPI) — subsidiary: 90.1%-owned subsidiary, acquired 4th July 2023; diversified the group's portfolio across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and consumer segments and strengthened technology capabilities in IMD, IMF and IML; transacts with the parent for sale/purchase of goods.
- Plastoranger Advanced Technologies Private Limited — subsidiary: Was a wholly-owned subsidiary of Walter Pack Automotive Products India Private Limited; amalgamated with WPI (the holding company) during the year pursuant to an order of the Regional Director under Section 233 read with Rule 25(5) of the Companies Act, 2013, and no longer exists as a separate entity.
- SJS Foundation — related party: A trust that is a related party of the Company (CSR-related trust); the Company does not have any holding/ultimate holding company, and has no associate or joint venture as at the end of the financial year.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: 2-wheeler: 38.3% of FY26 revenue, grew 4x industry; passenger vehicle: 41.7% of FY26 revenue, grew 3x industry; consumer & others: 20% of FY26 revenue, rationalized low-margin products, new high-margin programs ramping up

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Branding & Aesthetic Enhancements:** Self-adhesive labels (decals and body graphics), 2D and 3D appliques and dials, 3D luxury badges, domes, overlays and aluminium badges, Kromex badges, Capacitive overlays
- **Advanced Moulding & Finishing:** In-mould labels (IML), In-mould decorations (IMD), IMF, Illuminated Logos, Chrome-plated, printed and painted injection-moulded plastic parts
- **Precision Optical & Functional Components:** Lens mask assemblies, Optical plastics, Cover Glass & Displays (new category being added)

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: outperform industry by 1.5x–2x in FY27; margin: target 27–28% long-term; order inflow: strong pipeline across global OEMs; capex/commissioning: INR145Cr total capex planned over FY26–FY28 (INR80Cr done in FY26), including INR45Cr Bangalore expansion (20% capacity), INR100Cr SDPL chrome greenfield (commissioning complete), and display facility in Hosur (equipment ordered, production expected end-FY27/early-FY28)

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: BOE Varitronix optical display partnership (cover glass, TFT bonding) to unlock $4B global market; export expansion into Germany, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, South Korea; inorganic acquisitions in NA, SEA, India targeting margin-accretive players

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian decorative aesthetics industry estimated at ~Rs 49.2 billion in FY26, reflecting ~20% CAGR from FY 2020-21 amid premiumization across end-user segments, outpacing underlying volume growth in two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and durables (10-12% CAGR), driven by EV-specific trims, advanced coatings and manufacturing localisation (Source: Equity Edge Research)
- EV surge is a key market driver: electric models demand 1.5-2x higher aesthetic content (decals, chrome, IML) versus ICE vehicles, bolstered by PLI schemes and export growth
- Premiumization in appliances and sanitaryware, where durable, glossy finishes meet regulatory pushes for corrosion resistance and eco-compliance, is a growth driver
- Farm equipment mechanisation and capacity ramps are amplifying need for customised surface solutions amid a fragmented yet consolidating supply chain
- Industry is fragmented among niche specialists delivering end-to-end design-to-production; leaders with zero-debt profiles and EV-ready capabilities gain margin resilience and share in a globally underpenetrated, consolidating market
- Two-wheeler industry recorded highest-ever domestic sales in FY26 (10.7% growth), supported by GST 2.0, repo-rate cuts and income tax relief boosting consumer sentiment, with premiumisation (higher engine capacity, features) and rising EV segment uptick as sub-trends
- Passenger vehicle industry recorded highest-ever annual sales in FY26 (7.9% growth), with stronger growth in the second half of the year
- Rising demand for optical plastics/cover glass and display systems, as OEMs focus on design differentiation and higher content per vehicle, is supporting SJS's move into cover-glass and display manufacturing
- PV segment kit value is expected to grow from a legacy kit value of Rs 1,200-1,500 per vehicle, to a current kit value of Rs 3,500-5,000 per vehicle, with future kit value guided at 5-8x growth over the legacy level, as the product mix shifts to cover glass, digital displays, IMD/IML components and chrome-plated parts

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 30.3% due to premium product mix (24% of revenue from new-gen products), higher export contribution (60.5% YoY growth), operational efficiencies, and back-to-back cost pass-throughs on chrome plating inputs; polymer cost inflation mitigated by annual product refresh pricing

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priorities: 1) fund committed capex (INR220Cr), 2) retain dry powder (INR2,437M net cash) for inorganic acquisitions, 3) dividend payout of 35% of face value (INR3.5/share); no debt used, debt-free balance sheet maintained

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: SJS operates four existing manufacturing facilities across Bengaluru, Pune and Gurugram, with two new facilities coming up at Pune and Hosur to support capacity expansion and entry into a new product category. At SJS Decoplast (Pune), a chrome plating and painting capacity expansion (overall capex ~Rs 1,000 Mn) has been set up and is in its final stage of commissioning. A greenfield cover glass and automotive display facility is being established at Hosur (Phase I capital outlay ~Rs 650 Mn, including display system assembly); equipment has been ordered and revenue contribution is expected to begin from FY 2027-28. Capacity is also being expanded at the SJS (Bengaluru) plant (capex of Rs 400-450 Mn) to cater to a significant new business opportunity, with the expansion progressing well. Total capex investment across these projects was Rs 822.4 Mn (consolidated) in FY26. Growth has also come inorganically: the SJS Decoplast acquisition delivered revenue growth of 3.5x between FY 2020-21 and FY 2025-26, and the integration of Walter Pack India (WPI) diversified the portfolio across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and consumer segments and strengthened IMD/IMF/IML technology capabilities; management continues to evaluate further value-accretive M&A opportunities.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, bullish on FY27; emphasized disciplined execution, margin expansion, and strategic patience in export and inorganic growth; reiterated 26-year track record of outperformance; tone was assertive on technology leadership and operational excellence

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Design-to-delivery model and R&D/NPD capabilities (135-member NPD team) enabling entry into sophisticated, high-entry-barrier product categories with few competitors
- Manages over 17,500 SKUs with a diversified product portfolio, plant locations and customer base that spreads geographic and customer-concentration risk
- Long-standing customer relationships with key OEMs, some spanning nearly two decades
- Equipment/machinery flexibility across production lines and strict quality control at every stage to keep rejection rates low and avoid order delays
- AA-(Positive) long-term funds credit rating by ICRA, upgraded during the year from AA-(Stable)
- Technology Licence-cum-Supply Agreement with BOE Varitronix (BOEVX), Hong Kong for optical bonding and assembly of automotive display systems in India

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Global supply chain disruptions; geopolitical volatility affecting export markets; delay in BOE display product qualification; slower-than-expected ramp-up of new WPI programs; currency fluctuations impacting export profitability

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Export intensity is understated in consolidated figures — SJS standalone export contribution is significantly higher than reported due to SDPL/WPI being domestic-focused; BOE partnership is not just about displays but about vertical integration of aesthetic + electronic functions, positioning SJS as a holistic cabin experience partner

strategy.body:

- Innovating: focus on development of new technologies and advanced products, moving up the value chain into IMD/IML, IMF, hot stamping, optical plastics/cover glass and displays, and advanced decorative applications

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order book] Current order book to be executed in FY27 is over 88% of FY27 forecasted revenue; SJS expects to outperform underlying industry growth by 1.5-2x.
- [Exceptional item] Reported PAT includes a Rs 241.7 Mn exceptional gain — a one-time post-tax gain on sale of the Bangalore old facility, which was not in use since 2019.
- [Ownership] Aug'23 saw a stake sale of ~30% by PE promoter Everstone Capital, which had acquired a majority stake in 2015 with Serigraph exiting.
- [Governance] Board is chaired by a Non-Executive Chairman & Independent Director; the ESG annexure reports 57.14% independent board of directors and 16.7% founder board members.
- [Outlook wording] The FY27 outlook bullet reads 'Continue to maintain robust margin profile of business for FY26' — the deck refers to FY26 in an FY27 outlook slide.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

hero.oneLiner: SJS is a decorative-aesthetics and functional-component manufacturer with 39 years of expertise, supplying automotive (2W/PV) and consumer-appliance OEMs in India and abroad.
